all_misconceptions.population: first-semester general chemistry (GC1, N=83) and second-semester general chemistry (GC2, N=510) students
all_misconceptions.source_title: The Development of the Redox Concept Inventory as a Measure of Students' Symbolic and Particulate Redox Understandings and Confidence

all_misconceptions.target_misconception: Students think a combination reaction cannot be a redox reaction.
all_misconceptions.correct_answer_concept: A reaction can be both a combination reaction and a redox reaction if oxidation numbers change.
all_misconceptions.expected_reasoning: A student should determine whether oxidation and reduction occur by comparing oxidation states of reactants and products; if electron transfer/oxidation number changes occur, the reaction is redox regardless of being a combination reaction.
all_misconceptions.supporting_quote: "4Al(s) + 3O2(g) → 2Al2O3(s) is not a redox reaction because it is a combination reaction [3B, 4A]"
all_misconceptions.population: first-semester general chemistry (GC1, N=83) and second-semester general chemistry (GC2, N=510) students
all_misconceptions.source_title: The Development of the Redox Concept Inventory as a Measure of Students' Symbolic and Particulate Redox Understandings and Confidence

all_misconceptions.subtopic: Role of nitrate in single-displacement reactions
all_misconceptions.target_misconception: Students think NO3− is irrelevant in a single-displacement reaction because it cancels out in the net ionic equation.
all_misconceptions.correct_answer_concept: Nitrate is a spectator ion; it does not participate in the redox change, but it is still part of the original molecular equation and solution context.
all_misconceptions.expected_reasoning: A student should recognize that spectator ions remain unchanged on both sides and can be omitted from the net ionic equation, but they are not evidence that the species is irrelevant to the overall reaction setup.
all_misconceptions.supporting_quote: "In a single-displacement reaction of Cu(s) and AgNO3(aq), NO3− is irrelevant for the reaction because it cancels out in the net ionic equation [18D]"
all_misconceptions.population: first-semester general chemistry (GC1, N=83) and second-semester general chemistry (GC2, N=510) students
all_misconceptions.source_title: The Development of the Redox Concept Inventory as a Measure of Students' Symbolic and Particulate Redox Understandings and Confidence

all_misconceptions.subtopic: Bond breaking/forming as cause of electron transfer
all_misconceptions.target_misconception: Students think electrons transfer because ionic bonds break and form in a single-displacement reaction.
all_misconceptions.correct_answer_concept: Electron transfer is the defining feature of redox; in a single-displacement reaction electrons move from the metal that is oxidized to the ion that is reduced, not because bonds in the ionic compound simply break and reform.
all_misconceptions.expected_reasoning: A student should identify which species loses electrons and which gains electrons, then connect that transfer to oxidation and reduction. The bond-breaking/forming narrative does not explain the electron movement itself.
all_misconceptions.supporting_quote: "Electrons transfer because of ionic bonds breaking and forming in a single-displacement reaction [10A]"
all_misconceptions.population: first-semester general chemistry (GC1, N=83) and second-semester general chemistry (GC2, N=510) students
all_misconceptions.source_title: The Development of the Redox Concept Inventory as a Measure of Students' Symbolic and Particulate Redox Understandings and Confidence

all_misconceptions.subtopic: Electrons left behind when copper leaves the solid
all_misconceptions.target_misconception: Students think that when Cu2+ leaves the solid, two electrons remain behind on the solid.
all_misconceptions.correct_answer_concept: In the displacement reaction, copper metal is oxidized to Cu2+ by losing electrons, and those electrons are transferred to Ag+; they are not left stranded on the solid.
all_misconceptions.expected_reasoning: A student should track electrons through the half-reactions: Cu(s) → Cu2+ + 2e− and Ag+ + e− → Ag(s). Electrons are transferred to silver ions rather than remaining on the copper solid.
all_misconceptions.supporting_quote: "In a single-displacement reaction of Cu(s) and AgNO3(aq), when Cu2+ leaves the solid, two electrons remain behind [17D]"
all_misconceptions.population: first-semester general chemistry (GC1, N=83) and second-semester general chemistry (GC2, N=510) students
all_misconceptions.source_title: The Development of the Redox Concept Inventory as a Measure of Students' Symbolic and Particulate Redox Understandings and Confidence

all_misconceptions.subtopic: Silver replacing missing charge on copper solid
all_misconceptions.target_misconception: Students think Ag+ replaces the charge that is missing when Cu2+ leaves the solid.
all_misconceptions.correct_answer_concept: Ag+ does not replace a missing charge on the solid; it is attracted to electrons associated with the oxidation of copper and is reduced to Ag(s).
all_misconceptions.expected_reasoning: A student should reason that positive ions are reduced by accepting electrons, and the metal surface is not repaired by a charge-replacement process. The electron transfer drives the deposition of silver.
all_misconceptions.supporting_quote: "In a single-displacement reaction of Cu(s) and AgNO3(aq), Ag+ replaces the charge that is missing when Cu2+ leaves [16B]"
all_misconceptions.population: first-semester general chemistry (GC1, N=83) and second-semester general chemistry (GC2, N=510) students
all_misconceptions.source_title: The Development of the Redox Concept Inventory as a Measure of Students' Symbolic and Particulate Redox Understandings and Confidence

all_misconceptions.subtopic: Silver ions attracted to electrons left on the copper solid
all_misconceptions.target_misconception: Students think Ag+ ions are attracted to electrons left on the copper solid and then bond to the copper because of that attraction.
all_misconceptions.correct_answer_concept: Ag+ is reduced by gaining electrons from Cu(s); the process is electron transfer rather than silver ions bonding to copper because of leftover electrons on the solid.
all_misconceptions.expected_reasoning: A student should explain the reaction using oxidation and reduction: Cu loses electrons and Ag+ gains them. Attractive forces do not cause Ag+ to 'bond to the copper'; silver metal forms after reduction.
all_misconceptions.supporting_quote: "They're [Ag+(aq)] attracted to the electrons that are left um because of that copper leaving [Cu2+(aq)] , and then it [Ag+(aq)] needs to pick up two more so they're [Ag+(aq)] attracted to those electrons."
all_misconceptions.population: reported in validation interviews and used as the basis for distractor 16C
all_misconceptions.source_title: The Development of the Redox Concept Inventory as a Measure of Students' Symbolic and Particulate Redox Understandings and Confidence

all_misconceptions.subtopic: Two product argument for redox classification
all_misconceptions.target_misconception: Students think oxidation and reduction cannot both occur if there is only one product in the equation.
all_misconceptions.correct_answer_concept: The number of products does not determine whether a reaction is redox; redox is determined by oxidation number changes/electron transfer.
all_misconceptions.expected_reasoning: A student should inspect the oxidation states of Al and O in the reaction and recognize that Al is oxidized and O2 is reduced even though the equation has one product.
all_misconceptions.supporting_quote: "there is only one product, so oxidation and reduction cannot both occur"
all_misconceptions.prevalence: GC1/GC2 paired responses BA and BD were the two most frequent misconceptions; exact percentages not given
all_misconceptions.population: GC1 and GC2 students responding to two-tiered items 3 and 4
all_misconceptions.source_title: The Development of the Redox Concept Inventory as a Measure of Students' Symbolic and Particulate Redox Understandings and Confidence

all_misconceptions.target_misconception: Students think that because a reaction is a combination reaction, it is not redox.
all_misconceptions.correct_answer_concept: Combination reactions can be redox reactions if oxidation numbers change.
all_misconceptions.expected_reasoning: A student should use oxidation-state changes to classify the reaction, not the reaction type label alone.
all_misconceptions.supporting_quote: "they believed that 4Al(s) + 3O2(g) → 2Al2O3(s) is not a redox reaction because either 'it is a combination reaction'"
all_misconceptions.population: GC1 and GC2 students in two-tiered items 3 and 4; 27.7% GC1 and 22.4% GC2 selected this misconception category
all_misconceptions.source_title: The Development of the Redox Concept Inventory as a Measure of Students' Symbolic and Particulate Redox Understandings and Confidence
